mapping_diagnosis.distinguishing_reason: The story explicitly contrasts the fate of healthy vs. defective seeds under identical external conditions, making the internal condition (n3) and its enabling edge (e2) the most vivid and causally clear. The external condition (n2) and its edge (e1) are present but less emphasized as a necessary enabler because the story focuses on the failure of defective seeds despite good conditions, rather than on the success of healthy seeds requiring those conditions. A stronger realization would explicitly state that even healthy seeds cannot sprout without water, warmth, and air, thereby making the enabling role of n2 more explicit.

revision_instructions: To strengthen the mapping of edge e1 (external conditions enable germination), add a sentence such as: 'The old farmer knew that even the plumpest seed would never sprout if the soil were dry or cold.' This makes the necessity of external conditions explicit and balances the emphasis with the internal condition.
